items.title: Introduce transition-orchestrator.ts coordinating one transition
items.context: Create packages/main/src/handlers/transition-orchestrator.ts, not core/, because it coordinates handler-layer gate/effect modules (phase-gates.ts / transition-effects.ts / done-effects.ts) and a core/ file importing handlers/ would invert Core/Shell layering. It owns one transition's actor lifecycle, DONE merge lock scope, state mutation/writeStory ordering, pre/post gate ordering, and effect invocation. External CLI behavior and lifecycle semantics must remain unchanged (behavior-preserving explicit orchestrator). Note runDonePreMergeGate is gate-shaped (before actor.send) while applyDoneMergeEffects is effect-shaped (after writeStory phase=DONE) — the orchestrator must respect this straddling of the actor.send boundary.

items.title: Reduce story_advance.ts to a thin handler delegating to the orchestrator
items.context: story_advance.ts becomes a thin handler: parse CLI args, call transition-orchestrator, shape the response. It must no longer contain inline transition coordination, gate-runner bodies, or merge implementation. A thin handler means real delegation, not just moved comments. story-advance.ts line count drops substantially again.

items.title: Regression-prove zero CLI/semantics change and no circular imports
items.context: Extend smoke/contract coverage to prove: external CLI behavior (story_advance for every transition), TEST semantics, legacy phase handling, and workflow profile are all unchanged; the new modules have clear single responsibilities with no circular imports; StoryPhase / legacy phase types are untouched. Run build + flow-stability + validation-protocol + lifecycle-registry-contract + process-fact-contract + runtime-fact-contract + worktree-authority-smoke. Regression must prove behavior preservation while allowing internal ownership cleanup: no phase timing changes, no TEST/legacy/profile semantics changes, no circular imports, no global/shared hidden handoff.
